Heritage sites by state

Heritage sites in Tripura: Unakoti, Pilak and the Manikya palaces

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

Tripura's best known heritage sites are Unakoti, a hillside of giant rock-cut Shaiva reliefs of about the 8th to 9th centuries, and Pilak, where Buddhist and Hindu sculpture and a brick stupa base have been found. The Manikya kings left Ujjayanta Palace in Agartala and Neermahal, a water palace on Rudrasagar lake. Tripura has no UNESCO site.

We build Tripura study tours to Unakoti, Pilak and the Manikya palaces, with a sculpture identification session before your group sets out.

What makes Tripura's heritage distinctive

Tripura lies between Bangladesh and the hills of Mizoram and Assam, and its history reflects both. It was ruled for centuries by the Manikya dynasty, whose chronicle, the Rajmala, traces a long royal line, though its early parts are legendary. The plains around Udaipur and Agartala connected to Bengal, and the art at Pilak and Unakoti shows close links with eastern Bengal in the early medieval period.

Tripura also has nineteen recognised Scheduled Tribe communities, including the Tripuri, Reang and Jamatia, whose languages, weaving and festivals are a large part of the state's living heritage. Our guide to tribes of India gives the wider picture.

  • Pilak site area. Sculpture is displayed locally near the excavated mounds; check arrangements before visiting.

Unakoti: rock reliefs in the forest

Unakoti, in Unakoti district in the north of the state, is a forested hillside with huge reliefs carved into the rock faces and many smaller stone images. The best known is a giant head of Shiva, many metres high, with an elaborate headdress, flanked by female figures. Images of Ganesha, Durga and other deities are carved nearby. The work is usually dated to about the 8th to 9th centuries and is protected by the ASI.

The name means 'one less than a crore', from a legend that the images number just short of ten million. A spring festival, Ashokastami, draws pilgrims each year. Our lecture on rock-cut sacred architecture places Unakoti in the wider Indian tradition, and Reading sculpture teaches how to identify the figures.

Pilak: Buddhist and Hindu sculpture in south Tripura

Pilak, near Jolaibari in South Tripura district, is spread over a wide area of mounds and fields. Excavation has exposed the brick base of a stupa at Shyamsundar Tilla and found terracotta plaques and stone sculpture of both Buddhist and Hindu deities, including images of the Buddha, Avalokiteshvara, Surya and Vishnu. The finds are generally dated from about the 8th to the 12th centuries.

The mix of traditions at one site is the main lesson of Pilak. Our lecture on sacred architecture across communities uses examples like this to show how religious life overlapped in early medieval eastern India.

Palaces and temples of the Manikya kings

Ujjayanta Palace in Agartala, completed in 1901 for Maharaja Radhakishore Manikya, is a large white palace in an Indo-European style. It now houses the Tripura State Museum, with galleries on the state's history, communities and archaeology. Neermahal, built in the 1930s on Rudrasagar lake at Melaghar for Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya, combines Hindu and Mughal elements and is reached by boat.

The Tripura Sundari temple at Udaipur, the old capital, dates from the early 16th century and is an important Shakta pilgrimage site. Bhuvaneshwari temple, also at Udaipur, is linked with Tagore's writings on Tripura. Chhabimura, on the Gomati river, has rock carvings of deities on cliff faces seen from a boat.

Planning a heritage visit to Tripura

No Inner Line Permit is needed for Indian visitors. Agartala has an airport and rail link, Unakoti is a long drive north, and Pilak and Udaipur are to the south, so two or three bases work best. October to March is the comfortable season.

Questions people ask

What is Unakoti famous for?

Unakoti is famous for its giant rock-cut reliefs on a forested hillside in north Tripura, including a huge head of Shiva flanked by female figures and images of Ganesha and Durga. They are usually dated to about the 8th to 9th centuries and are protected by the ASI.

What has been found at Pilak?

Pilak in South Tripura has the brick base of a stupa and many terracotta plaques and stone sculptures of Buddhist and Hindu deities, including the Buddha, Avalokiteshvara, Surya and Vishnu, mostly of about the 8th to 12th centuries.

Are there UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Tripura?

No. Tripura has no UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its major heritage places are Unakoti, Pilak, Ujjayanta Palace, Neermahal and the temples of Udaipur.

What is Neermahal?

Neermahal is a water palace in the middle of Rudrasagar lake at Melaghar, built in the 20th century for Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya. It mixes Hindu and Mughal architectural ideas and is reached by boat.
